390.name: New to Oath & Action
Designing a piece
Building with code
Find out what Oath & Action does and what our four pillars, Explain, Track, Connect and Act, each stand for. Chapter 01 Purpose
Check the label above a headline to see what kind of piece you are reading. Rule 01.21 Purpose
When we take a side on a measure, the piece opens with the label “Our position” and gives the strongest case against it. Rule 01.23 Purpose
The evidence grade beside a claim, from documented to hypothesis, tells you how sure that claim is. Rule 02.22 Voice
Read the word Illustrative as our sign that the item beside it is invented. Rule 02.22 Voice
See how a tracker follows a bill through six numbered steps, from filing to the governor’s or president’s desk. Rule 11.1 Status and utility icons
Every piece ends on one step you can take, with its date and the way to take it. Rule 02.24 Voice
Choose the lockup, our name and marks set in one fixed arrangement, by the width you have and the surface it sits on. Rule 03.2 Identity
Start on Newsprint, our warm off-white page, and set text only on color pairs with enough contrast. Chapter 05 Color
Spend red on one job in each view, such as the step a reader can take now. Rule 05.3 Color
Take every type size from the type scale, and set nothing on screen under 13 px. Rule 06.2 Type
Space the page with the 8 px spacing scale, on the column grid for its width. Chapter 07 Layout and spacing
See the identity at true size on four of our pieces, from the site’s masthead to a letterhead. Appendix Identity proofs
Download tokens.css and tokens.json, which hold the same tokens under one version number. Rule 26.8 Tokens and how to choose them
Link tokens.css before your own styles, then give the body its margin and type. Rule 26.5 Tokens and how to choose them
Choose each token in five steps, starting from the surface it sits on. Rule 26.3 Tokens and how to choose them
Let the page follow the reader’s light or dark setting through one attribute on its root. Rule 26.6 Tokens and how to choose them
Copy each control’s code from chapter 18, where every control works by keyboard and screen reader. Chapter 18 Components and interaction
Give each of the ten states, from hover to error, words or a shape as well as a color. Rule 17.8 Motion and states
Before you call a page finished, run the checks in chapter 19 against WCAG 2.2 at level AA, the accessibility standard we build to. Rule 19.7 Accessibility
